original_source_text: Stochastic computing (SC) enables compact and low-complexity hardware but remains underexplored for vision applications. We propose EdgeSC, a unified stochastic framework that extends edge detection to diverse and composite operators. Pixel intensities are encoded as stochastic bitstreams, and gradients are computed through finite-state machines (FSMs) ensembles operating in the probability domain. A differentiable MUX mapping learns operator-specific behaviors without changing the architecture. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, EdgeSC achieves 15.9$\times$ smaller area, 4.4$\times$ lower power, and 6.3$\times$ better area-delay product than 8-bit baselines while maintaining comparable accuracy and throughput.
